title: The Bridge That Twisted Itself Apart

claims.source: WSDOT / FHWA Tacoma Narrows Bridge History
claims.note: Opened to traffic July 1, 1940 spanning The Narrows of Puget Sound, Washington.
Center suspension main span measured 2,800 ft (total structure length 5,939 ft, deck width 39 ft).
Used solid 8-ft plate stiffening girders along a narrow 39-ft two-lane roadway.

claims.source: FHWA / University of Washington wind-tunnel investigation
claims.note: Motion transitioned from vertical undulation to self-exciting aeroelastic torsional flutter around 10:03 a.m. on Nov 7, 1940.
Approximately 600 ft of the center roadway span tore free and plunged into Puget Sound at ~11:02 a.m., Nov 7, 1940.
No human deaths occurred; engineers and motorists evacuated safely before span separation.
